query: Which concrete tests and numeric thresholds will detect pre-event drift or information leakage (e.g., cumulative ARs in [-10,-2], abnormal volume, event-day order-flow)?

response.query: Which concrete tests and numeric thresholds will detect pre-event drift or information leakage (e.g., cumulative ARs in [-10,-2], abnormal volume, event-day order-flow)?
response.answer: Pre-event drift detection includes monitoring abnormal volume and order-flow changes, with numeric thresholds like cumulative abnormal returns in [-10,-2]. Tests include statistical analysis of order-flow anomalies and volume spikes.

results.title: programa de pós-graduação em geografia - Brasília - SIGAA UnB
results.content: ), which leads to an increase in precipitation, the distribution of rain and the intensity of the wind, which, combined with the topography of the country, the characteristics of the soil and the increase in population in coastal areas, generates a greater risk from hydrometeorological threats. The general objective of this work is to analyze the occurrence of extreme hydrometeorological events in Costa Rica and identify the risks and impacts of floods in the country. This work presents two parallel and complementary approaches, one of a climatological nature that analyzes precipitation in the Tempisque River basin in its temporality and spatiality, statistically analyzing pluviometric data through climatological analysis; On the other hand, the risks associated with extreme rainfall events and their impacts during hurricanes Eta and Iota in 2020 are investigated, through the analysis of biophysical data recorded by meteorological stations belonging to the IMN, satellite images and precipitation maps, reports from the National Emergency Commission and the Municipality of Santa Cruz, records of reports made to the 911 emergency system and news, which allow identifying the main vulnerabilities of Santa Cruz against extreme hydrometeorological events.
